title: Siege of Changchun
summary: In 1948 Communist forces besieged Changchun in Manchuria and refused to let civilians leave while the city's food had been requisitioned by the Nationalist garrison. A Communist broadcast reported the Nationalist Sixtieth Army turning on 17 October, and a US telegram reported the city fallen by 22 October. Civilian starvation deaths are estimated at about 150,000 to 300,000; no official toll exists.

uncertainty.note: Sources date the blockade from late May 1948 and the siege as May to October; Du Bin counts from 4 November 1947. The final collapse is dated 17 October (Sixtieth Army uprising) to 19-22 October.

as_recorded.value: Kmt Sixtieth Army uprose against Kmt in Changchun yesterday

importance.justification: A siege by starvation that decided Manchuria for the Communists and killed a very large number of civilians, long left out of official history.

audience_note: Describes mass starvation of civilians during a military blockade. Death figures are contested estimates and there is no official count.

beats.caption: Communist forces besieged Changchun from May 1948; a PLA officer later wrote that civilians starved there until October.
A Communist broadcast said the Sixtieth Army turned on the New Seventh Army inside Changchun on 17 October; a US telegram reported the city fallen by 22 October.
Estimates of civilians who starved range from about 150,000 to at least 300,000; no official toll has been published.
